title: Projector cone cancels the unwanted binomial summands
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U\subset X$ open, and $R:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_U)$ the canonical restriction [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $s\in\mathbf N$, $F\in D(\mathcal O_U)$ and $A\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ with $R(A)\cong\bigoplus_{j=0}^{s+1}F[j]^{\oplus\binom{s+1}{j}}$. Then there exists $\alpha:R(A)\to R(A)$ such that, for every $A^{\prime}$, $\gamma:A^{\prime}\to A$, isomorphism $b_U:R(A^{\prime})\cong R(A)$ with $\alpha=R(\gamma)\circ b_U^{-1}$, and distinguished triangle $A^{\prime}\xrightarrow{\gamma}A\to E\to A^{\prime}[1]$ [def-weil-triangulated-category], one has $R(E)\cong F\oplus F[1]$.

proof.text: For a finite family H indexed by J with a chosen j0, take a distinguished cone triangle of zero on H(j0) and of identity on H(j) for every j unequal to j0. Mathlib distinguished_cocone_triangle constructs the triangles and Triangle.isZero3_of_isIso1 shows that every identity cone is zero. Their product is distinguished by Mathlib productTriangle_distinguished.

The projection from the product of cones to its j0 component is an isomorphism: its inverse has the identity in that component and zero elsewhere; product extensionality and zero-ness of the other components prove both inverse laws. Rotate the zero-map triangle; its third arrow is zero. The split triangle lemma identifies its middle term, namely the chosen cone, with H(j0) plus H(j0)[1].

In the binomial index type choose j0=(0,0); the second coordinate is valid since choose(s+1,0)=1. Transfer the first arrow of the product triangle to R(A), using the supplied biproduct isomorphism and biproduct.isoProduct. This defines alpha.

Restriction takes the supplied distinguished triangle to a distinguished triangle. The equation alpha=R(gamma) composed with bU inverse gives an isomorphism of its first arrow with that of the constructed product triangle. Mathlib isoTriangleOfIso12, using the triangle-morphism isomorphism criterion, identifies their third objects. Compose with the cone calculation and the shift-by-zero isomorphism to obtain R(E) isomorphic to F plus F[1].
